faq.a1: A standard company registration typically takes 3 to 4 weeks at normal processing speed, provided all required documents are prepared and apostilled where necessary. This covers registration with the Ministry of Commerce, tax registration with the GDT and NSSF enrollment. EP Partners manages this entire process for clients from start to finish.
faq.a2: Cambodia does not impose a general minimum capital requirement for most sectors. However, certain regulated industries — banking, insurance, microfinance, and others — have specific minimum registered capital requirements set by their respective regulators. For standard trading, consulting, and service companies, the registered capital is set by the shareholders and is commonly set at USD 10,000–100,000 depending on operational needs.
faq.a3: Yes, foreigners can own 100% of shares in a Cambodian company in most business sectors. The primary restriction relates to land: foreign entities cannot own land in Cambodia directly. Businesses requiring land use typically structure through long-term leases (up to 50 years, renewable), co-ownership with a Cambodian national, or a concession agreement.
faq.a4: A typical company operating under the Real Regime tax system is subject to: Value Added Tax (VAT) at 10%, monthly Tax on Income (ToI) prepayment at 1% of turnover, annual Tax on Income at 20% of net profit, Withholding Tax on applicable payments, and Patent Tax (annual business license fee). Payroll-related taxes include NSSF contributions for all employees.
faq.a5: Yes. EP Partners provides full audit representation services, including preparation of audit responses, document gathering, liaison with GDT officers, and negotiation of any assessments. We also offer proactive pre-audit health checks to identify and remediate compliance gaps before a formal audit is initiated.
faq.a6: Our team is fluent in English, Khmer, and Mandarin. We provide all client services, documents, and communications in the client's preferred language. This trilingual capability is particularly valuable for our Chinese-speaking clients from mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan who are establishing or operating businesses in Cambodia.
